BiblicalUsage: Azekah was a town in the low country of Judah, named in the wars of Joshua, in the muster against the Philistines at Shochoh, and in the last stand of the cities Nebuchadnezzar took before Jerusalem fell. The Philistines camped between Shochoh and Azekah when Goliath came out, and Joshua's men pursued the five kings down to Azekah under the great hailstones.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Azekah's story is the story of a border town that saw both victory and defeat, and I hold that God was in both — the hailstones at Joshua's battle and the long siege at Jeremiah's.
